note: Irregularities and unverified items found during this build. None block publication.

flags.title: Demo API not reachable from the build sandbox
flags.observed: The agent sandbox that built this repository has no network route to *.kalshi.co: TLS is closed (SSLZeroReturnError) and DNS resolves but the handshake never completes. The official docs pages were reachable, so documentation was verified directly.
flags.impact: All live collection therefore runs on GitHub Actions (collect.yml / probe-api.yml), which do have egress. The repository's committed data is produced there.

flags.title: Demo environment prices are not production prices
flags.observed: Kalshi's own demo guide states: "The price and behavior of markets in the demo environment may not be reflective of those in real markets."
flags.impact: Every number on this site is a demo-environment number. It is labelled as such in the header and footer, and must not be read as a production price.

flags.title: WebSocket API requires an authenticated handshake
flags.observed: The official WebSocket guide states that connections require authentication during the handshake, and that even public market-data channels use the authenticated session.
flags.impact: A purely static, credential-free web page cannot hold a WebSocket. The dashboard therefore uses REST polling (browser live reads + committed snapshots). True streaming requires the demo credentials, which this session cannot create.

flags.title: Signed REST calls from a browser are subject to CORS preflight
flags.observed: Signed requests must send KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY, KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE and KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP headers. A cross-origin browser request with custom headers triggers a preflight, and the allowed header list is controlled by Kalshi, not by this project.
flags.impact: Live *signed* reads (balance, positions, order entry) are therefore performed server-side in GitHub Actions, not in the visitor's browser. The probe records the exact preflight response in data/verify-api.json so the current behaviour is measured rather than assumed.

flags.title: No demo API credentials in this session
flags.observed: KALSHI_DEMO_API_KEY_ID / KALSHI_DEMO_PRIVATE_KEY are repository secrets that only the repository owner can create; none were present.
flags.impact: Demo-account balance, positions and order execution are implemented but untested end to end. portfolio.json says configured=false and the performance page says so explicitly. Simulated (paper) trading does run and is fully tracked.

flags.title: Fee schedule: formula note vs printed table
flags.observed: The fee schedule PDF says the fee is rounded up "such that the fee + positionCost is rounded to a centicent" ($0.0001). Every value in the PDF's own General Trading Fees Table is reproduced only by rounding up to the next whole cent. Example: 1 contract at $0.50 → formula gives $0.0175, table prints $0.02.
flags.impact: The engine defaults to cent rounding (which matches all 42 printed values, asserted by tests/test_fees.py) and records the rounding rule in every trade's fee_model field. Sub-cent markets could differ; flagged for review.

flags.title: Volume is reported in contracts, not dollars
flags.observed: Market objects expose volume_fp / volume_24h_fp as contract counts. There is no traded-dollar field on the market object.
flags.impact: "Highest dollar amount" ranking uses est_volume_24h_dollars = volume_24h_fp × last price, which is an estimate and is labelled as one in data/meta.json and on the dashboard.

flags.title: Gas topic: crude-oil series carry the same tags
flags.observed: Kalshi's `Oil & Gas` / `Oil and energy` tags also cover series such as "North Dakota crude oil production", which are not retail gasoline prices.
flags.impact: An explicit exclusion (KXNDKOIL) is recorded in collector/topics.py with its reason, rather than a silent filter. Other crude series may need the same treatment; review the matched series list on the Gas topic page.

flags.title: No verified news-attribution feed
flags.observed: The brief asks which events or links may have caused a jump of ≥ $0.10. This project has no verified, official news source that can be tied to a specific contract move.
flags.impact: No causal claim is made anywhere on the site. Each alert links to its own API row and market page so a human can investigate. Adding attribution would require a news API and an explicit correlation method.

flags.title: Resolution state depends on live-endpoint availability
flags.observed: Kalshi partitions data into live and historical tiers; settled markets older than the `market_settled_ts` cutoff stop appearing in GET /markets and move to GET /historical/markets.
flags.impact: A market that settles while the collector is paused could be missed by the live poll. The tracker keeps its own record of every market it has seen, so a missing row is visible as `awaiting_result` rather than being silently dropped. Historical fallback is documented but not yet wired in.

flags.title: Repo review: repository contained only a one-line README
flags.observed: At commit 003447e the repository held a single file, README.md, containing "# Tradebot2". There was no code, no license file, no CI configuration and no Pages content; Pages was enabled on main and served an empty site.
flags.impact: There was nothing to review line by line, so this build is additive. Findings are recorded in the README's "Repo review" section. No other session had a claim on the task board.

flags.title: Scheduled GitHub Actions runs are best-effort
flags.observed: GitHub documents that scheduled workflows can be delayed and are disabled automatically after 60 days of repository inactivity.
flags.impact: The 5-minute cadence in collect.yml is a target, not a guarantee; gaps appear as wider spacing on the charts and in run_log.json timestamps. The site never back-fills a gap.

flags.title: Sub-cent price grids are supported by the API but not exercised here
flags.observed: The fixed-point docs list markets with 0.001 / 0.0001 tick sizes (e.g. multivariate, some crypto series). The dashboard's y axis and delta arithmetic handle them, but the tracked demo markets observed in this session used $0.01 grids.
flags.impact: A $0.10 threshold is unaffected by tick size, but fee rounding on sub-cent markets could differ from the cent-rounded model (see F-06).

flags.title: Topic rules cover categories and tags, not individual contract wording
flags.observed: Series metadata (category / categories / tags) is used to assign a topic. A contract whose wording implies a topic but whose series metadata does not carry a matching tag would not be picked up.
flags.impact: This is deliberate: matching on title keywords would be inference. The matched series list is published per topic so a missing series is easy to spot and add to collector/topics.py.
